name: De Mores company office and store (NPRC store, post office, meat market, offices)
evidence: Photographed winter 1883-84 (houghton:3013533); labelled "company store" in the 1919 panorama. Former carriage-house store room (Cow Boy 1884-05-15); plank sidewalk in front of "the Co's stores" (1885-02-05); Howe scales in front of the offices (1885-06-25); NPRC general offices moved here from St. Paul, Oct 1885.

name: Medora Hotel (Coleman & Brown boarding house and restaurant)
evidence: Lot bought June 19, 1884; nearly done July 3; ad Nov 20, 1884 (Cow Boy).

name: Company barn, stable and corral (Deffebach livery)
evidence: Rented to Bassie Deffebach as a livery (May 1884); additional barn south of the old one (March 1885) (Cow Boy).

name: Gill Kennedy's oyster restaurant
evidence: Building moved from the west side to John Warn's old lot, Sept 1885; ice-house south of it (Cow Boy).

name: John O'Sullivan's barber shop and house
evidence: Lot 11, Block 19 (Cow Boy 1885-09), "next to John Warn's" restaurant. Block 19 is not in today's parcel layer.

name: McKenzie & O'Brien blacksmith shop
evidence: Moved to the north side of the track, May 1885; sold to Alex Morton 1886 (Cow Boy).

name: W. B. Pryor's shoe shop
evidence: On a lot "near the church," March-April 1885 (Cow Boy).

name: E. Grymes's brick dwelling
C. F. Ellison's house by the Catholic church
evidence: Cow Boy, Nov-Dec 1885.

name: NP coal mine and powder house
evidence: Coal mine roof caving in (Cow Boy 1884-06-12); old powder-house north of the track.

name: Merchants National Bank (planned)
evidence: Four lots at the corner of Third Street and Broadway bought April 1884; again planned "on the vacant hotel square" in 1885; never reported built (Cow Boy).

name: Medora Stage & Forwarding Co. office, warehouse and baggage room
evidence: Line ran Oct 1884-May 1885 (HMdb 88033, 303699). Three buildings on a triangular block beside the tracks and old US 10, west of De Mores Park; in 1957 one stood on its original site and two had been moved a few feet (BROOKS57 pp. 19, 22 and Fig. 8). Place from the 1957 Tour map once it is fitted.

name: Medora school
evidence: "A new school building has been erected" (Bismarck Weekly Tribune 1885-11-20); photo shsnd:00042-00037 "new schoolhouse".

name: Stockyards
evidence: Old NP yards "across the river" were too small; a small yard 50x50, then 100x100 (Cow Boy 1885-04-16); new yards at "the brick-kiln butte" with the river, butte and railroad as pen walls (Oct 1885).

name: Paddock's building for the Boston clothing house
evidence: Nearly finished June 1885 (Cow Boy 1885-06-25); Paddock's residence moved to Dickinson in sections June 1887.

name: Sylvane Ferris's house
evidence: Two-story section with bay window and porch wing (shsnd:00129-00012).

name: De Mores rental houses ("Houses to be let")
evidence: shsnd:00042-00030 etc.; St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13 mentions "numerous small residence houses."

name: De Mores brick business block (planned)
evidence: Two store rooms below, offices above (St. Paul Daily Globe 1884-02-13). Was it built?

name: Railroad shipping corrals
evidence: "the shipping corrals near the Cantonment" (HAG).

name: Gifford Bros. & Co. general store, Little Missouri
evidence: To open June 1883 (Dickinson Press 1883-06-16).

name: Other 1883 Little Missouri saloons (Smith & Stevens; Edgar & Saebastian; J. J. Smith)
evidence: Dickinson Press ads, July 1883.

name: Paddock's cabin and livery, Little Missouri
evidence: "'Little Misery.' Paddock's cabin in foreground, 1880" (Haynes, in NPSHB).
